```{r}
# Install libraries
install.packages("dplyr")
install.packages("readr")
install.packages("ggplot2")

# Load libraries
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
```

```{r}
#-------------------------------------
# Step 1: Read and inspect the database
#-------------------------------------

# Load database
df <- read.csv("Health-Lifestyle Dataset.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Display how many rows and columns the database have
cat("Numbers of rows:", nrow(df), "\n")
cat("Numbers of columns", ncol(df), "\n\n")

# Display columns names
cat("Columns Names are:\n")
print(names(df))

# Display first 5 rows of the database
print ('First rows of the dataset:')
print(head(df, 5))
# -------------------------------------
```

```{r}
# Check how many missing value per column
cat("Nmber of missing values in each column:\n")
print(colSums(is.na(df)))

# Check how many missing value per row
rows_with_na <- sum(!complete.cases(df))
cat("\n Number of rows that contain missing values:", rows_with_na, "\n")
```

```{r}
#-------------------------------------
# Handle missing data
#-------------------------------------
df[] <- lapply(df, function(x) {
  # Check whether column is text
  if (is.character(x)) { 
    x <- trimws(x)       # remove extra spaces
    x[x == ""] <- NA     # convert empty string "" to NA
  }
  return(x)
})

# Categorical
## Impute missing values with mode (most common value
Mode <- function(x) names(which.max(table(x)))

# Replace missing values with mode)
df$Occupation[is.na(df$Occupation)] <- Mode(df$Occupation)
df$BMI.Category[is.na(df$BMI.Category)] <- Mode(df$BMI.Category)
df$Sleep.Disorder[is.na(df$Sleep.Disorder)] <- Mode(df$Sleep.Disorder)
df$Blood.Pressure[is.na(df$Blood.Pressure)] <- Mode(df$Blood.Pressure)

# Check how many missing value per column
cat("Nmber of missing values in each column:\n")
print(colSums(is.na(df)))

```
```{r}
#-------------------------------------
# Step 2: Descriptive statistics 
#-------------------------------------

# Blood Pressure must be split into systolic and diastolic
df$Systolic <- as.numeric(sub("/.*", "", df$Blood.Pressure))
df$Diastolic <- as.numeric(sub(".*/", "", df$Blood.Pressure))

# Define categorical and numerical columns
categorical_columns <- c("Gender", "Occupation", "BMI.Category", "Sleep.Disorder")
numerical_columns <- c("Age", "Sleep.Duration", "Quality.of.Sleep", "Physical.Activity.Level", "Stress.Level", "Heart.Rate", "Daily.Steps", "Systolic", "Diastolic")

# Print descriptive statistics for numerical variables
cat("Descriptive Statistics for Numerical Variables:\n")
for (col in numerical_columns) {
  cat(paste("\n", col, "Descriptive Statistics:\n"))
  print(summary(df[[col]]))   # Summary statistics (mean, median, range, etc.)
  cat("Standard Deviation: ", sd(df[[col]], na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
}

# Print frequency tables for categorical variables
cat("\nFrequency Tables for Categorical Variables:\n")
for (col in categorical_columns) {
  cat(paste("\n", col, "Frequency Table:\n"))
  print(table(df[[col]]))  # Frequency table for categorical variables
  cat("\n")
}

```
```{r}
#-------------------------------------
# Step 3: Plot numeric variables (histograms)
#-------------------------------------
# List of numeric columns to plot
numeric_vars <- c("Age", "Sleep.Duration", "Physical.Activity.Level",
                  "Stress.Level", "Heart.Rate", "Daily.Steps")
# Layout for 6 plots
par(mfrow=c(2,3))

# Create a histogram for each numeric variable
for (v in numeric_vars) {
  hist(df[[v]], main=paste("Histogram of", v),
       xlab=v, col="lightblue", border="black")
}

# Reset layout
par(mfrow=c(1,1))

```
```{r}
#-------------------------------------
# Step 4: Relationship of Age, Stress, Physical Activity with Blood Pressure
#-------------------------------------

# Simple linear regression (systolic)
model <- lm(Systolic ~ Age + Stress.Level + Physical.Activity.Level, data=df)
summary(model)
```
```{r}
#-------------------------------------
# Step 5: Correlation with Heart Rate
#-------------------------------------

# Convert gender + occupation to numeric codes
df$Gender.num <- as.numeric(as.factor(df$Gender))
df$Occupation.num <- as.numeric(as.factor(df$Occupation))

# Correlations with Heart.Rate
cat("Correlation between Gender (numeric) and Heart Rate:\n")
print(cor(df$Gender.num, df$Heart.Rate, use="complete.obs", method = "pearson"))

cat("\nCorrelation between Occupation (numeric) and Heart Rate:\n")
print(cor(df$Occupation.num, df$Heart.Rate, use="complete.obs", method = "pearson"))

cat("\nCorrelation between Daily Steps and Heart Rate:\n")
print(cor(df$Daily.Steps, df$Heart.Rate, use="complete.obs", method = "pearson"))

cat("\nCorrelation between Age and Heart Rate:\n")
print(cor(df$Age, df$Heart.Rate, use="complete.obs", method = "pearson"))

```
```{r}
# Plot correlations
par(mfrow=c(2,2))
plot(df$Gender.num, df$Heart.Rate, main="Gender vs Heart Rate")
plot(df$Occupation.num, df$Heart.Rate, main="Occupation vs Heart Rate")
plot(df$Daily.Steps, df$Heart.Rate, main="Daily Steps vs Heart Rate")
plot(df$Age, df$Heart.Rate, main="Age vs Heart Rate")
par(mfrow=c(1,1))
```
```{r}
#-------------------------------------
# Step 6: robability BMI = Normal given Occupation and Gender
#-------------------------------------
# 1. P(BMI = Normal | Occupation = Doctor)
doctor_subset <- df[df$Occupation == "Doctor", ]
mean(doctor_subset$BMI.Category == "Normal", na.rm = TRUE)
```

```{r}
# 2. P(BMI = Normal | Gender = Male)
male_subset <- df[df$Gender == "Male", ]
mean(male_subset$BMI.Category == "Normal", na.rm = TRUE)
```
```{r}
#-------------------------------------
# Step 7: Outliers in Sleep Duration
#-------------------------------------
boxplot(df$Sleep.Duration, main="Sleep Duration Boxplot")
```
```{r}
# Detect outliers
sleep_outliers <- boxplot.stats(df$Sleep.Duration)$out
sleep_outliers
```
```{r}
#-------------------------------------
# Step 8: Correlation with Sleep Disorder
#-------------------------------------
# Convert Sleep Disorder into numeric
df$SleepDis.num <- as.numeric(as.factor(df$Sleep.Disorder))

cat("Correlation between Blood Pressure and Sleep Disorder:\n")
cor(df$Systolic, df$SleepDis.num, use="complete.obs", method = "pearson")
cat("\n")

cat("Correlation between Sleep Duration and Sleep Disorder:\n")
cor(df$Sleep.Duration, df$SleepDis.num, use="complete.obs", method = "pearson")

```

```{r}
# Graphical representation
plot(df$Systolic, df$SleepDis.num,
     main="Blood Pressure vs Sleep Disorder")
plot(df$Sleep.Duration, df$SleepDis.num,
     main="Sleep Duration vs Sleep Disorder")
```
